headline: Rally outruns a still-fearful tape ahead of the Trump-Xi summit
body: Equities are grinding to fresh records even as the underlying mood gauge stays defensive: the Nasdaq Composite jumped roughly 2.3% Monday to a record close and futures were little changed to modestly higher heading into Tuesday, but CNN's Fear & Greed Index sits at 29 — solidly in Fear territory, only a few points off the 26 low it touched last week. That gap traces back to the Fed's September 16 move to lift its target range to 3.75%-4%, its first hike since 2023, which left positioning cautious even as price action turned bullish. The proximate spark for the rally has been a sharp pullback in crude, down roughly 9% over four sessions, on hopes that renewed US-Iran diplomacy eases Middle East supply risk, taking some pressure off the inflation narrative that drove the Fed's hand in the first place.

The other pillar under the tape is Thursday's Trump-Xi summit in Washington, with Treasury Secretary Bessent calling weekend preliminary talks in New York 'very successful' and investors pricing in an extension of the trade truce alongside possible AI-cooperation signals. Semiconductors and AI infrastructure names continue to lead, with Nvidia trading within a few points of its record high on continued hyperscaler capex and Blackwell demand. Retail-sentiment trackers show the usual concentration of chatter in mega-cap AI and momentum names but no distinct new narrative beyond what's already driving price action, so today's read leans more on macro catalysts and index moves than on any fresh social-chatter signal. Net effect: a market pricing in relief on two fronts, oil and US-China trade, while sentiment surveys have yet to catch up to the tape.
